stories.title: Aave and Lido Lose $1.7 Billion in DeFi Capital Drop After Binance Hack
stories.summary: A Binance hack triggered a sharp pullback in DeFi lending and staking. Aave and Lido together lost $1.7 billion in deposited capital in the aftermath. The drop shows how fast confidence can leave major protocols once an exchange is breached.
stories.whyItMatters: Capital flight from two of DeFi's largest protocols signals contagion risk that can spread well beyond the exchange where the hack happened.
whatToWatch: Whether deposits return to Aave and Lido in the coming days
Any details Binance releases about the hack's scope and cause
Signs of further contagion to other DeFi protocols
questions: How much of the $1.7 billion was withdrawn, and how much was lost in value?
What exactly happened in the Binance hack?

sources.title: Aave and Lido lose $1.7B in massive DeFi capital drop after the Binance hack

stories.title: Weekend Stock Tokens Predict Monday's Open, But Betting on a Rise Wins Only 55% of the Time
stories.summary: Tokenized stocks that trade over the weekend give an early read on how a stock will open Monday. A review found that simply betting prices will rise is correct only 55% of the time, barely above a coin flip. The finding questions how useful these weekend prices really are as a signal.
stories.whyItMatters: Traders increasingly watch weekend stock tokens for clues on Monday's market, so weak predictive power matters for anyone relying on them.
whatToWatch: Whether accuracy improves or worsens as weekend stock-token trading volume grows
questions: What sample size and time period produced the 55% figure?

sources.title: Weekend stock tokens predict Monday open, but guessing up scores 55%

stories.title: Nvidia Stock Tokens Show Price Spreads, But Slippage Crushes the Arbitrage
stories.summary: Tokenized Nvidia shares trade at prices that diverge from the underlying stock, creating apparent arbitrage opportunities. In practice, slippage and execution costs eat up most of the potential profit. The gap points to a difference between tokenized-stock price quotes and real trading conditions.
stories.whyItMatters: It tempers hype around tokenized equities by showing that listed price gaps don't translate into easy, risk-free trades.
whatToWatch: Whether liquidity improves enough to narrow the gap between spreads and slippage
questions: How large were the observed spreads compared to typical slippage costs?

sources.title: Nvidia stock tokens show price spreads, but slippage crushes the arbitrage

stories.title: Bitcoin Tops $80,000 for First Time Since Binance Hack, But History Warns of a Crash
stories.summary: Bitcoin rose above $80,000 for the first time since the Binance hack rattled markets. The rally came despite a Democratic sweep in recent elections, a result some expected to unsettle crypto. Commentary around the rally pointed to past patterns that preceded earlier crashes.
stories.whyItMatters: A recovery above $80,000 after a hack-driven selloff is a key sentiment signal, but the crash-pattern warnings call for caution over hype.
whatToWatch: Whether Bitcoin holds the $80,000 level in the coming sessions
Any further market reaction tied to the election results
questions: What specific historical pattern is being cited as a crash warning, and how reliable is it?

sources.title: Bitcoin rockets above $80,000 for first time since Binance hack despite Democrats sweep, but a historical crash looms

stories.title: Bitcoin Miners' Revenue per Unit of Computing Power Falls 8.7%
stories.summary: Bitcoin miners' daily revenue for each unit of computing power, a measure called hashprice, fell 8.7%. The decline squeezes miner profit margins and reflects shifts in network difficulty, hashrate, or bitcoin's price. It points to tightening economics across the mining sector.
stories.whyItMatters: Falling miner revenue can pressure smaller or less efficient miners and affect the economics behind network security over time.
whatToWatch: Whether hashprice stabilizes or keeps falling in the coming weeks
Any resulting shifts in miner hashrate or capitulation
questions: What drove the 8.7% drop: bitcoin's price, difficulty, or fees?

sources.title: Bitcoin miners’ daily revenue per unit of computing power falls 8.7%

stories.title: Pro-Crypto Candidates Win 241 Seats as Congress Shifts Power
stories.summary: Candidates described as pro-crypto won 241 seats in recent elections, a result reported as a shift in the balance of power in Congress. The outcome suggests a more favorable environment for digital-asset legislation. It was not specified which chamber or how the count was defined.
stories.whyItMatters: Congressional composition shapes the pace and direction of US crypto regulation, including market-structure and stablecoin bills.
whatToWatch: Which crypto-related bills gain momentum under the new Congress
Committee assignments and leadership tied to digital-asset policy
questions: How was 'pro-crypto' defined, and across which races was the count taken?

sources.title: Pro-crypto candidates sweep 241 seats as Congress shifts power

stories.title: Polkadot Loses $1.38 Million After Hacker Exploits a Flaw Patched Four Months Earlier
stories.summary: A hacker exploited a security flaw in the Polkadot ecosystem that had already been fixed four months earlier, causing a $1.38 million loss. The incident suggests the earlier fix was not applied everywhere it needed to be. It adds to a recent run of crypto security incidents.
stories.whyItMatters: An old, already-patched flaw causing a new loss points to gaps in how security fixes propagate across a protocol's ecosystem.
whatToWatch: Whether Polkadot or affected parties recover any of the stolen funds
Confirmation of why the earlier patch didn't cover this exploit path
questions: Which specific component or chain within the Polkadot ecosystem was hit?

sources.title: Polkadot lost $1.38 million after hacker exploited security flaw fixed four months earlier

stories.title: Kamino Ties Most of CEO's Token Vesting to Valuation, Leaving Holders Without a Claim on Foundation Revenue
stories.summary: Kamino structured most of its CEO's KMNO token vesting around the token's valuation rather than protocol performance. Meanwhile, KMNO holders reportedly have no claim on revenue held by the project's foundation. The setup raises questions about how well the CEO's incentives align with those of token holders.
stories.whyItMatters: Vesting and revenue-claim structures matter to token holders, since misaligned incentives can hurt token value even as insiders profit.
whatToWatch: Whether Kamino responds to the vesting structure or adjusts its terms
Any community or governance pushback from KMNO holders
questions: What share of the CEO's vesting is valuation-linked versus performance-linked?
Why do holders have no claim on foundation revenue?

sources.title: Kamino links most of CEO’s KMNO vesting to valuation while holders have no foundation revenue claim

stories.title: US Stock Perpetuals Get the Green Light, But Market Halts Could Still Trap Traders
stories.summary: Perpetual futures contracts tied to US stocks have won regulatory clearance to trade. But because the underlying stock market can halt trading, holders of these contracts could still be unable to exit positions during a halt. The clearance marks a notable step for derivative equity products built on crypto market infrastructure.
stories.whyItMatters: It shows crypto market-structure products moving into traditional equities, but the halt risk shows the mechanics aren't fully resolved.
whatToWatch: How exchanges handle open perpetual positions during an underlying stock halt
Trading volume once US stock perpetuals launch more broadly
questions: Which regulator granted the clearance, and what conditions came with it?

sources.title: US stock perpetuals win clearance, but stock-market halts can still block exits

stories.title: Evernorth's XRP Funding Plan Could Raise $18 Million Less at a Lower Share Price
stories.summary: Evernorth's plan to raise funds tied to XRP could bring in $18 million less than originally expected, because of a lower share price. The shortfall reflects weaker terms than the company had anticipated for the raise. It's a setback for one of the XRP-linked funding efforts in the market.
stories.whyItMatters: A smaller-than-planned raise limits how much capital an XRP-focused venture can deploy and may signal softer investor demand.
whatToWatch: Whether Evernorth adjusts the deal size or terms
Confirmation of the final raise amount once the deal closes
questions: What caused the share price to come in lower than planned?

sources.title: Evernorth’s XRP funding plan could raise $18 million less at lower share price
